abstract_sentences.text: Midtraining, the practice of mixing specialized data with more general pretraining data in an intermediate training phase, has become widespread in language model development, yet there is little understanding of what makes it effective.

evidence.anchor: Midtraining, the practice of mixing specialized data

abstract_sentences.text: We propose that midtraining functions as distributional bridging by providing better initialization for post-training.

We conduct controlled pretraining experiments, and find that midtraining benefits are largest for domains distant from general pretraining data, such as code and math, and scale with the proximity advantage the midtraining data provides toward the target distribution.
In these domains, midtraining consistently outperforms continued pretraining on specialized data alone both in-domain and in terms of mitigating forgetting.

We further conduct an investigation on the starting time and mixture weight of midtraining data, using code as a case study, and find that time of introduction and mixture weight interact strongly such that early introduction of specialized data is amenable to high mixture weights, while late introduction requires lower ones.
This suggests that late introduction of specialized data outside a plasticity window cannot be compensated for by increasing data mixtures later in training.
Beyond midtraining itself, this suggests that distributional transitions between any training phases may benefit from similar bridging strategies.

evidence.anchor: may benefit from similar bridging strategies

experimental_design.name: model family and pretraining budget
experimental_design.description: Pythia 70M-1B models are trained from scratch on C4 for 128B tokens, about 61k steps, with cosine schedule and AdamW.

experimental_design.name: midtraining interventions
experimental_design.description: Five mixtures span Starcoder code, Math, FLAN instructions, KnowledgeQA, and DCLM; Table 1 lists their sources and token amounts.

experimental_design.name: control condition
experimental_design.description: C4-only continued pretraining receives the same number of tokens with other training details held identical.

experimental_design.name: downstream tasks
experimental_design.description: GSM8K, SciQ, CodeSearchNet-Python/Pycode, and LIMA span the covered domains and receive standard language-model SFT.

experimental_design.description: Catastrophic forgetting is evaluated as cross-entropy loss on held-out C4 after SFT.

experimental_design.name: proximity diagnostic
experimental_design.description: PA uses unigram token statistics under the model tokenizer; Appendix D defines the mixture-aware combined score.

experimental_design.name: seeds and hyperparameter selection

final_judgment.single_storyline: Midtraining is presented as a distributional bridge: a retained general-data mixture shifts initialization toward a distant target before SFT, which is associated with lower target loss, better C4 retention, and smaller late-layer change.
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: The main body keeps definitions, research questions, five Findings, Table 2/3, Figure 3/4, and a CKA exemplar, enough to decide whether the empirical pattern holds in the tested regime.
final_judgment.appendix_moves: Proofs, hardware and hyperparameters, full similarity calculation, complete 70M-410M loss table, representative curve, and CKA extensions move to the appendix. This preserves a short main narrative but makes mechanism rigor and reproducibility appendix-dependent.
final_judgment.best_pattern: Use an operational bridge diagnostic, then triangulate it with a cross-domain table, a direct alternative comparison, and a timing-weight grid. Table 2 and Figure 3 make baseline, direction, and encoding explicit.
final_judgment.largest_gap: Gradient alignment is central to the theory but never directly measured; PA and CKA are proxies. The continued-pretraining comparison changes start time, the 70M correlation differs between text and figure, and seed dispersion is absent.
final_judgment.transfer_rule: For a distribution-transition paper, tie each causal link to a stated intermediate state, a downstream outcome, a nearest-alternative control, and a documented failure boundary in the main evidence chain.
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: When the intermediate state is only a token-overlap or representation proxy, state an empirical association rather than a verified optimization mechanism unless a direct mediator measurement or matched causal intervention is supplied.
